source_excerpts.text:
Existing physical construction
Krings, McManigal and Markvicka2025 uses a damage-created conductive network as a local heater and subsequently opens it electrically. Its actual main manufacturing/validation was read at the scope recorded below. The actuator demonstration depressurises before healing and uses re-pressurisation without visible water leakage as its reported functional observation. Electrical coupon reset cycles and a whole actuator's repeatable useful-load life are distinct quantities. The source is credited as prior construction; cited material stability and other cited-original results remain secondary exposure only.

source_excerpts.text:
Independent introduced two-location model
Two ohmic elements are in series under0.5A. In stateA the wound bridge is9ohm and an intact lead1ohm; stateB exchanges their physical locations. Both thermal nodes have C0.25J/K, G0.01W/K and ambient25C, with no thermal cross-coupling. Their temperature is
T(t)=25+I^2*R/G*(1-exp(-G*t/C)).
An introduced local opening threshold200C acts at whichever element is hot. Under these declared assumptions both circuits have identical5V/0.5A electrical histories, open at37.6019349s and consume94.0048373J before opening. Yet the wound is200C inA and44.4444C inB.

A separate introduced closure law, dx/dt=0.5*(1-x) when woundT>=160C and zero otherwise, gives x0.9993557 versus0. This law is not measured polymer kinetics, restored strength or a signal available to the controller. Its role is to show that identical terminal reset can coexist with different physical outcomes. Resistance-temperature changes, cross-coupling and actual electromigration require a different calibrated model. This is a scoped terminal-only counterexample, not an all-sensor impossibility theorem.

An optional direct local-voltage observation would break the pair: with introduced±0.05V error, wound voltage intervals are[4.45,4.55]V and[0.45,0.55]V. At current>=0.49A their local power lower bounds are2.1805W and0.2205W. A real four-terminal or segmented implementation must identify and span the correct damaged region while its leads survive. It requires actual wiring, geometric and calibration contracts; assumed voltage taps do not supply them. Local heating evidence still does not establish material repair or useful force.

After opening, the introduced hot node requires48.6478s to cool from200 to50C with the same G and C. A vanished electrical short does not by itself make a hot softened structure ready to carry load. This is not a prescribed temperature limit or a measured cooldown time.

source_excerpts.text:
Independent introduced gas proof
A second model integrates ideal-gas mass loss through an isentropic-orifice surrogate with discharge coefficient0.65, gamma1.4 and R287.05J/kgK. The initial isolated stock is10mL at150kPa absolute and298.15K against100kPa ambient. No pump supplies replacement gas during the5s test.

In the rigid isothermal case, equivalent circular radii1,2,5 and10um give pressure drops29.3437,117.3249,731.0959 and2893.1366Pa. These are surrogate holes, not measured cracks or a calibrated leak-valve curve. At2um, adding a uniform0.1K warming and V(p)=V0*(1+kappa*(p-p0)) with introduced kappa5e-6/Pa reduces the pressure drop to38.3408Pa. Two endpoint sensors each with±50Pa error can contribute±100Pa to their difference. The isothermal rigid117Pa signal cannot simply be transferred to a compliant warming actuator.

The model uses
dp/dt=[-R*T*mdot+(p*V/T)*dT/dt]/[V+p*dV/dp].
This retains mass accounting under declared volume compliance and an imposed temperature ramp. Actual creep, shape changes, heat gradients and measurement uncertainty remain outside it. Conservation of p*V/T can help formulate a diagnostic only when the relevant temperature and volume are actually observed or bounded. A pressure proof also cannot establish strength, actuation force, fatigue life, interlayer adhesion or restored critical material stocks.
